newsitem.title: HUNGARY: FORECAST - Hungary bond, T-bill yields seen dropping.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Hungary bond, T-bill yields seen dropping.

text.p: Hungarian government bonds and Treasury bill yields were seen continuing to ease on the secondary market this week, but at a slower pace than last week, dealers said on Tuesday.

Dealers said that according to estimates, year-on-year inflation dropped below 20 percent in December, and this low level caused government paper yields to slump late last week, following bond auctions on Thursday.
"There was a drastic enough fall," said Zsolt Bango of Gog Securities, adding that yields on the secondary market dropped by 100 to 150 basis points last week.

One- and three-month T-bills were sold at 21.6 to 21.7 percent, six- and 12-month bills at 21 to 21.3 percent. Government bonds with 1998 maturities were traded at between 20.5 and 20.7 and three-year bonds between 20.3 and 20.4 percent.
Dealers said that the easing of Hungary's overnight rates this year from 26.5 percent to below 22 percent showed that the liquidity of banks improved rapidly since the year-end.
Increasing demand on better liquidity and the recent decline of inflation should push the yields down further by some 30 basis points, they added.

Bango said he primarily expected the six- and 12-month T-bills and the three-year bonds to drop as he saw strong demand for these papers, adding that three-year yields may drop below 20 percent within a few days.
